generatedFor: Spirit / Pitaya — theological university, single student
notes: v3 — final. Context correction: Michael's church is IBCC Cali, a daughter church of Grace Community (MacArthur) — his PULPIT is dispensational while his bookshelf (Sproul, Voddie) is covenantal and his first nine years were charismatic. Term 3 rebuilt as a map-not-verdict comparison. Eschatology named as a live burn: his instinct is amil/postmil renewal-not-escape; Year 3 gives it Terms 28, 31, 34. Year 3 (terms 25-36) now fully planned. Retained from v2/v2.1: cap 15, full Year 1 replace, homework schema, no Spanish-language term.

authorGuidance.breatherEveryThree: At least one term of 10 studies or fewer in every rolling window of three terms.
authorGuidance.hardSpacing: Terms whose hard flags mark morally distressing content should not be adjacent. Doctrinally-contested hard flags are exempt. Planning guidance only — do not enforce in the importer.

sit.label: Sit with it
sit.description: One question carried through the day. No answer required, no writing. The point is that it follows you into the car and the kitchen.

read.label: Read one more
read.description: A second passage, read whole, with no commentary and no study notes. Usually a cross-reference, the text being quoted, or the passage that complicates today's.

research.label: Find one thing out
research.description: A custom, a word, a place, a date, a person. Logos and the Reformation Study Bible are the intended tools. Must have a floor: one specific findable thing, never an open-ended rabbit hole.

write.label: Leave a trace
write.description: A paragraph, a paraphrase in his own words, a list, a letter he never sends. Never longer than a paragraph. Used sparingly so it stays weighty.

compare.label: Two translations
compare.description: The same verse in ESV and NBLA, sometimes NASB or KJV. Note what shifts. This is where the Spanish lives now. Comparison, not immersion.

ask.label: Bring it to someone
ask.description: Bring one question to one person: Kat, his dad, Jonathan, Benjamin, a pastor. Not evangelism, not a witnessing assignment. A question asked out loud to someone who knows him. Year 2 onward only.

generatorRules: Exactly one homework item per study.
Never repeat the same homework kind on two consecutive days within a term.
Draw only from the kinds listed on that unit.

REQUIRED: every study opens by naming the previous study's homework in one line before teaching anything. This is the mechanic that keeps a lesson from evaporating. Do not skip it on day 1 of a term; reference the last day of the previous term instead.
Homework never requires a purchase, a website he does not already have, or leaving the house.
A 'write' item never asks for more than one paragraph.
The curriculum is a spiral: when a unit's refs revisit an earlier term's ground, say so naturally in one clause (e.g. 'you mapped this in Term 28'). Callbacks are load-bearing, not decoration.

terms.title: Reading the Room
terms.kick: METHOD · what question was the writer actually answering?
terms.rationale: We start with how to read, because everything after this depends on it. You already believe that a text answers the question its writer was asking, and that forcing it to answer yours is a kind of theft. You have just never studied that conviction on purpose. So we will. Romans 9, where almost everyone helps themselves. Ruth 4, where the man without a name is the point. Matthew quoting Hosea in a way no seminary would allow. Learn the discipline now and it protects the next three years.
terms.secondNote: This term encodes the method behind The Grafted. If the group ever restarts, this is its syllabus.
terms.homeworkArc: Keep one page. Every time you catch yourself wanting a verse to say something, write the verse down. Do not argue with yourself yet.

terms.title: Genesis: The Promise Under Everything
terms.kick: NARRATIVE · the covenant everything else stands on
terms.rationale: You hold covenant theology and you have never studied the covenants. That is the gap we close first. Before Sinai, before David, before the cross, there is a man told to leave his country and a God who walks alone between the pieces of a slaughtered animal. Every argument you want to have later, about Israel, about baptism, about the church, runs back through Genesis 15 and 17. So we go there first and slowly, and we leave the argument for the next term.
terms.hardNote: Genesis 22 is read whole. A father, a son, a knife, and no explanation offered until the last moment. It is not softened here.

units.label: The first promise, spoken to a snake

terms.title: Covenant and Dispensation: The Map
terms.kick: DOCTRINE · your pulpit holds one, your bookshelf holds the other
terms.rationale: You asked for definition, and now I know the actual shape of the question. Your bookshelf is covenantal: Sproul and Voddie. Your pulpit is dispensational: IBCC is a daughter of Grace Community. You sit under one system and read under the other, and you are not yet deep enough in either to say precisely where they part. So this term is a map, not a verdict. Both systems at full strength from their own texts, then the downstream: what each does to Israel, to baptism, to the end of the world. Your instinct can survive definition. Find out.
terms.hardNote: The unit called The System in Your Pew reads dispensationalism the way its best men teach it, your own elders among them. No caricature, no Left Behind. If you cannot state their case so they would sign it, you have not finished the unit.
terms.secondNote: Two honest cuts, one per side. Aim the Scofield apprehension precisely: the pretribulational rapture SYSTEM is 19th century (Darby, then Scofield 1909), but premillennialism itself is ancient — Justin and Irenaeus held it. And covenant federalism is likewise a post-Reformation systematization; Hosea 6:7, a favorite covenant-of-works proof text, turns on a disputed rendering (like Adam / at Adam) and must not carry weight alone. Precision cuts both directions or it is not precision.
terms.homeworkArc: Two columns, one page. Every argument that actually landed on you, from either side. Write it down even when it lands wrong.

units.label: The new covenant, promised out loud

terms.title: The One Another Church
terms.kick: PRACTICE · the warmth you said your doctrine did not give you
terms.rationale: You told me something worth taking seriously: that your charismatic roots loved better than your Reformed convictions do, and that you feel the lack. So we put it here, early, before the long study terms. Not a doctrine of sanctification. Just the commands, read plainly, with nowhere to hide behind precision. Philippians 2 first, because it is the mind of Christ and it goes downward. Then a towel, then John's letter, which will not let you call yourself loving in the abstract.
terms.secondNote: Your instinct that they love better is worth taking seriously, and it is not an argument for their doctrine. Both can be true. Hold both.
terms.homeworkArc: Once a week, name one person you have privately written off. Do not act yet. Just name them.

units.label: Love that is not a feeling

terms.title: The Gospel of Mark
terms.kick: GOSPEL · who do you say that I am
terms.rationale: Mark is the shortest and the fastest and the one that refuses to explain itself. No genealogy, no birth, no infancy. He starts at full speed and he asks one question for sixteen chapters. Everything before Caesarea Philippi builds the question. Everything after it walks toward a cross. And then he ends without an ending, which is either a scribal accident or the most demanding conclusion in the New Testament. We will look at both. Read it as the first readers did, in a hurry, and unsettled.
terms.hardNote: The passion narrative is read whole. Gethsemane, the trial, the flogging, the cry of dereliction. No compression.

units.label: The temple and the fig tree

terms.title: Justification
terms.kick: DOCTRINE SHORT · declared, not made
terms.rationale: Six days. You know this doctrine well enough to recite it and that is exactly the risk. So we go slowly through the courtroom language, and then we let James complicate it in the last study, because a doctrine you cannot let anyone press on is not a conviction, it is a reflex. Paul confronting Peter to his face is the middle of the term for a reason. This truth was worth a public fight between apostles. It should cost you something to hold.

terms.title: The Judges
terms.kick: NARRATIVE · everyone did what was right in his own eyes
terms.rationale: Twelve studies, not forty two. This book does not need length, it needs nerve. Judges is the account of a people who kept being rescued and kept forgetting, told by an author who refuses to editorialize and simply shows you what happened. It gets worse as it goes. By the end there is a dismembered body and a civil war and a line that explains the whole book. We are not skipping those chapters. They are the argument.
terms.hardNote: Judges 11 and Judges 19-21 are read whole: a daughter sacrificed on a vow, a concubine given to a mob and cut into twelve pieces, and a tribe nearly erased. These are in your Bible on purpose. They are not sanitized here and they are flagged before you arrive.
terms.homeworkArc: A running list, one line per study: what did Israel lack, and what did they reach for instead.

units.label: A vow he should not have kept
A Levite, a concubine, a war

terms.title: Romans 1-8
terms.kick: EPISTLE · the argument, first half
terms.rationale: Half of Romans, twelve studies, and we stop at chapter 8 on purpose. Chapters 9 to 11 are not an appendix and they are not a treatise on election, and you will read them properly next year with the covenant work behind you. For now: the courtroom, the two men, the death you already died, the war in chapter 7 that Christians have argued about for sixteen centuries, and then the chapter that ends with nothing being able to separate you. Take it slowly. It was written to be read aloud.
terms.secondNote: Stopping at chapter 8 is deliberate. Romans 9-16 is Term 21, after Reading the Room and Covenant and Dispensation have done their work.

terms.title: Giving a Reason
terms.kick: WITNESS · and the methods that disagree with each other
terms.rationale: Count the room. Sproul, Craig, Lewis, and Huff all reason from evidence toward God. Voddie argues that nobody is neutral and the case starts on Christian ground or it does not start. You are five to one classical and you did not choose that, you absorbed it. Before you pick a method, read the texts underneath both instincts. Then notice that Paul preaches one way in Jerusalem and another in Athens, which is Term 1 arriving to complicate whichever preference you were about to settle into.
terms.secondNote: Sproul co-wrote Classical Apologetics, subtitled a critique of presuppositional apologetics. Voddie leans on Bahnsen and Van Til. Two men Michael trusts published against each other on this exact question. Say so plainly. Wesley Huff's manuscript work is a third species, evidential rather than philosophical, and it already threads through Term 5 (Mark's longer ending) and Term 11 (canon).

terms.title: The Exile
terms.kick: HISTORY & PROPHETS · when the promise looked broken
terms.rationale: The single most disorienting event in the Old Testament. The temple burned, the king blinded, the land emptied. Everything God had promised, visibly undone. The prophets are not background here, they are the interpretation. Jeremiah tells them to build houses in Babylon, which is the least comforting comfort in Scripture. Psalm 137 ends the way it ends and we are not cutting the last verse. This term teaches you how to hold a promise while it is being contradicted in front of you.
terms.hardNote: 2 Kings 25 and Lamentations 1 are read whole, and Psalm 137 includes verse 9. The Bible does not close its eyes to what was done to that city or what the survivors wished on their enemies.

terms.title: The First Five Centuries
terms.kick: CHURCH HISTORY · with the Bible open the whole time
terms.rationale: The church spent four hundred years working out how to say what it already believed, and it cost people their lives to get the wording right. Nicaea was not a committee inventing a doctrine, it was a fight over whether John 1 means what it says. Every study here anchors to the text they were arguing about, including Proverbs 8, which Arius used and which orthodox readers had to answer honestly. History taught this way is not trivia. It is watching people read your Bible under pressure.
terms.hardNote: Proverbs 8:22-31 is read whole alongside John 1. It is the text Arius used and it does not become easy just because he lost.

units.label: Was there a time he was not

terms.title: Hope: The Last Things
terms.kick: DOCTRINE SHORT · what you are actually waiting for
terms.rationale: Six studies to close the year, and they land here on purpose. You now have the covenant framework, so eschatology can be studied instead of fought about. We stay off the timeline charts entirely. What we do instead is look at the return, the judgment, the body raised, and the city coming down, and then finish with what waiting is supposed to do to a man in the meantime. Titus 2 is the last study because hope that changes nothing about Tuesday is not the hope Paul meant.
terms.hardNote: Revelation 20:11-15 and Matthew 25:31-46 are read whole. Judgment is not softened, and the sheep and goats will press on you in a way you should let it.
terms.secondNote: Timeline questions are deferred on purpose. Year 3 draws the four maps (Term 28) and walks Revelation with them in hand (Term 31). This term is about the object of hope, not the sequence of it.

units.label: He will come the same way

terms.title: The Psalms by Kind
terms.kick: POETRY · the book that teaches you how to pray
terms.rationale: You finished a year of doctrine without once studying the prayer book God wrote. That was the largest gap in Year One and we open Year Two by closing it. Psalms are sorted by kind here, not by number, because a lament and a hymn are different instruments and playing one like the other ruins both. The cynic in you is going to find lament surprisingly hospitable. That is not a loophole. It is a licensed vocabulary that Scripture gives you on purpose.
terms.hardNote: Psalm 88 ends in darkness with no resolution, and it is read whole without a comforting appendix. The imprecatory psalms, including Psalm 137:7-9 and Psalm 109, are read whole. They are prayers, they are inspired, and they are not sanitized here.
terms.homeworkArc: Write your own lament, one line a day. Do not resolve it. Do not tidy it. It stays open until the praise unit.

units.label: How to read a poem that prays
Praise that has been through something

terms.title: Prayer: The School of Asking
terms.kick: PRACTICE SHORT · the disciples only asked him to teach them one thing
terms.rationale: Six studies, placed right after the Psalms while the vocabulary is still fresh. Notice what the disciples never asked for. Not how to preach, not how to heal. Teach us to pray. This term stays practical and short and it does not build a system. Gethsemane is in the middle because the most important prayer ever prayed was not answered the way it was asked, and any theology of prayer that cannot hold that is a theology for people who have not needed one yet.
terms.homeworkArc: Pray one of the term's passages back, out loud, once a day. Nothing added.

terms.title: The Spirit and the Gifts
terms.kick: DOCTRINE · why caution, and why not condemnation
terms.rationale: You asked how to be careful here without being contemptuous, and that is the right question, because contempt is the easy version and it is usually pride wearing doctrine. We read 1 Corinthians 12 and 14 whole, including the parts that both camps skip. We look honestly at what the sign gifts were for and whether that purpose still stands. And we end on the test that is not doctrinal at all, which is fruit, because you already suspect the people you disagree with are sometimes bearing more of it than you are.
terms.hardNote: 1 Corinthians 14 is read entire, including the passages each side habitually truncates. If a verse cuts against your position, it stays in.
terms.secondNote: Say this plainly in the term: your sense that they love better is an observation worth keeping and it is not evidence for their doctrine. Do not resolve the tension by discarding either half. Nine of his years happened in charismatic rooms. They are family, not a case study — the term should sound like a man examining his own house, not touring someone else's.

units.label: The test that is not doctrinal

terms.title: The Gospel of John: Seven Signs
terms.kick: GOSPEL · these are written so that you may believe
terms.rationale: Mark asked who this is. John tells you at the start and then spends twenty chapters proving it with seven signs and seven I AM statements, and he says outright in chapter 20 why he selected them. This is the most structured gospel and the most theological, and it is the one to read after a year of doctrine because you will finally see the architecture. Water into wine at the front, a dead man walking out of a tomb at the back, and a purpose statement in between.

units.label: In the beginning was the Word

terms.title: Providence and Suffering: Joseph and Job
terms.kick: NARRATIVE & DOCTRINE · you meant it for evil
terms.rationale: Two men, opposite structures. Joseph gets an explanation at the end and gives it himself in one sentence that has carried more suffering people than almost any other. Job never gets one. God answers him with a whirlwind full of questions and no reasons, and Job is satisfied. Put them side by side and you get the actual doctrine of providence, which is not that suffering is explained but that it is governed. Read the friends carefully. They are almost right, and that is the warning.
terms.hardNote: Job 1-2 is read whole, including the heavenly scene Job himself is never shown. The friends' speeches are read as written, not corrected in advance. This book does not resolve comfortably and we do not force it to.
terms.secondNote: William Lane Craig's Molinism offers a genuinely different account of how God governs a world containing evil, via middle knowledge and libertarian freedom. Michael leans on Craig and calls himself Reformed. On providence these are not compatible. Present Molinism accurately and at its best, do not strawman it, and let him feel that he is choosing rather than inheriting.

units.label: The wager you were not shown
The friends who were almost right
I know that my Redeemer lives

terms.title: Proverbs: Wisdom for a Working Man
terms.kick: WISDOM · the book written for someone with a job
terms.rationale: You run operations. You build systems. You handle money, hire people, manage a calendar, and lose your temper occasionally. Proverbs was written for exactly that man. Eight studies, deliberately practical, and we finish with the unit most people never get: what a proverb is not. A proverb is a probability, not a promise, and treating Proverbs 22:6 as a guarantee has wrecked more parents than almost any other misread. That last study is Term 1 coming back to collect.

terms.title: The Reformation
terms.kick: CHURCH HISTORY · the argument you inherited
terms.rationale: You call yourself Reformed. This is where that word comes from and what it cost. Twelve studies, Bible open the entire time, because the Reformation was fundamentally an argument about texts. But we are not telling it as a hero story. The unit on Zurich is flagged hard, because the Reformers drowned Anabaptists over believer's baptism, which is the position you now hold. Your own tradition has blood in it. Knowing that should make you a more careful man, not a less convinced one.
terms.hardNote: The Zurich unit covers the Reformers' persecution and execution of the Radical Reformers over believer's baptism. It is told honestly, including that men you admire signed off on it.

terms.title: The Confessions Compared: WCF and 1689
terms.kick: DOCTRINE · read the document you say you hold
terms.rationale: You describe yourself as conversant with the 1689. This term makes that true and raises the stakes. Westminster is the document R.C. Sproul spent his life teaching. The 1689 is the one you say you hold. The Baptists kept Westminster's wording wherever they could agree, which makes every difference precise and impossible to blur. Chapter seven on covenant, and the baptism chapters, are where they part, and those are exactly where your Term 3 questions landed. Same argument, one level deeper, in documents rather than personalities.
terms.homeworkArc: One paragraph, written at the end: what do you actually confess, in your own words, without quoting either document.

terms.title: Romans 9-16
terms.kick: EPISTLE · the half you were not ready for last year
terms.rationale: Here is the payoff. You now have Reading the Room, you have the covenants, you have the confessions. So read Romans 9 the way Paul wrote it, which begins with him in anguish and wishing himself cursed for his kinsmen, not with a systematician building a doctrine of election. The election is genuinely there. It is just not the question he set out to answer. Hold both. Then chapters 12 through 16 land, and it turns out the whole argument was going somewhere practical the entire time.
terms.hardNote: Romans 9:6-29 is read whole, vessels of wrath included. Do not soften the potter, and do not let the potter erase Paul's grief in verses 1 to 5.
terms.secondNote: This is where the Term 1 method meets the hardest passage in Scripture. Note the sharp edge honestly: Sala's audience-and-occasion method, applied consistently to Romans 9, pushes toward a corporate reading of election that sits closer to Craig than to Sproul. Michael should feel that pressure. Do not resolve it for him.

terms.title: Killing the Flesh
terms.kick: PRACTICE · mortification, which is not a metaphor
terms.rationale: Year One gave you the one another commands. This term goes underneath them to the thing that keeps blocking them, which you named yourself: arrogance, cynicism, the need to be the sharpest man in the room. Scripture does not ask you to manage that. It uses the language of execution. Put to death. Crucified. The eye and the hand. Eight studies, and the tax collector at the back of the temple is near the end because his prayer is seven words long and you already know you cannot pray it honestly on a good day.
terms.hardNote: Matthew 5:27-30 is read whole. The hyperbole is real hyperbole and it is also more serious than the word hyperbole makes it sound.
terms.homeworkArc: Once a week, write down one thing you said that was accurate and unkind. Accuracy is not the defense you keep treating it as.

terms.title: Hebrews: Better in Every Way
terms.kick: EPISTLE · written to people about to quit
terms.rationale: Hebrews only works after the covenant terms, which is why it waited two years. This is a letter to Jewish believers considering going back, and its entire argument is comparative: better than angels, better than Moses, better than Aaron, a better covenant, a better sacrifice, once for all. It is also the letter with the warning passages that have troubled serious Christians for two thousand years, and we are not going to defuse chapter 6 with a footnote. You will sit in it.
terms.hardNote: Hebrews 6:1-12 is read whole and left standing. Whatever your view of perseverance, the warning is addressed to the church and it is meant to be felt.

units.label: Better than Moses, and a rest

terms.title: The Attributes of God
terms.kick: DOCTRINE · closing the year on the subject, not the system
terms.rationale: Two years of studying about God. This term studies God. Ten days, one attribute at a time, always from a text where he shows it rather than a definition where someone summarizes it. Exodus 34 appears twice on purpose, once under justice and once under mercy, because it is the same sentence and it says both, and you will not be allowed to keep only the half you prefer. We end at Deuteronomy 29:29, on the line between what is hidden and what is given.
terms.hardNote: Exodus 34:6-7 is read entire, including the visiting of iniquity to the third and fourth generation. Nahum 1 is read as written. The severity is not edited out to make the mercy easier.

terms.title: Apologetic Methods Compared
terms.kick: WITNESS · three schools, one gospel
terms.rationale: Year Two ended with God himself. Year Three opens with the argument about how anyone comes to know him. Here is the room you have been standing in without noticing: Sproul, Craig, Lewis, and Huff all reason from evidence toward God. Voddie says nobody is neutral and the case starts on Christian ground or nowhere. Sproul and Bahnsen published against each other on exactly this. Proverbs, remarkably, contains both methods in two consecutive verses. Read the texts under each school, then stand in Athens one more time and pick your opening move — loosely.
terms.secondNote: Name the literature: Classical Apologetics (Sproul, Gerstner, Lindsley) against Van Til and Bahnsen; Craig's kalam and resurrection case; Huff's manuscript evidentialism; Lewis's moral argument as classical-adjacent. The Proverbs 26:4-5 pair is the presuppositionalists' own two-step — give it to both sides.

units.label: Sproul against Van Til: the family fight
Pick your opening move, hold it loosely

terms.title: Acts: The Church Breathing
terms.kick: NARRATIVE · what the Spirit actually built
terms.rationale: You have studied the Spirit and the gifts. Now watch what the Spirit actually built. Acts is the church breathing: three thousand at a sermon, property sold freely and one couple struck down for lying about it, a persecutor blinded into an apostle, a Gentile soldier praying while heaven forces Peter's hand. Watch the council in chapter fifteen especially — the first time the church had to decide what the covenant means for outsiders, a question you have been circling for three terms. They settled it with Scripture, testimony, and a letter.
terms.hardNote: Acts 5 and Acts 7 are read whole: a couple struck dead over a lie about money, and a man stoned while praying for his killers. Luke does not soften either, and neither do we.

units.label: The fellowship, and the first crack

terms.title: The Sermon on the Mount
terms.kick: GOSPEL · the kingdom's ethic, preached to the powerless
terms.rationale: The kingdom's ethic, preached on a hillside to people who had no power. You told me you struggle with the idea that this world simply ends. Good — the Sermon assumes it doesn't: the meek inherit the earth, not the clouds. But this is also the hardest text in Scripture for a sharp-tongued, pragmatic man: anger as murder, enemies loved, righteousness done in secret where nobody can be impressed by it. Two houses at the end, one storm. Here your instinct about heaven and earth gets its feet held to the fire.

units.label: Salt, light, and the law fulfilled

terms.title: Four Maps of the Millennium
terms.kick: DOCTRINE · eschatology without hysteria
terms.rationale: Now the term your last message asked for. Four maps of the end: dispensational premillennial, which your church holds; historic premillennial, which Justin and Irenaeus held; amillennial, which Augustine and Sproul held; postmillennial, which the Puritans dared to hold. Your instinct — renewal rather than escape — has a name and a lineage, and you should know which one before you claim it. We read the Day of the LORD where the language starts, Olivet with the Term One method, the rapture text in its own context, and Revelation twenty under all four maps at once.
terms.hardNote: Matthew 24 contains the sentence 'this generation will not pass away,' which is doctrinally hard for every map, including yours. It is read whole and no reading is allowed to skip it. Every map is drawn by its own cartographers at full strength — the one preached from your pulpit especially.
terms.secondNote: Keep the target precise: his skepticism of outlandish eschatology was formed in charismatic prophecy culture — date-setting, blood moons, headlines. His church's careful futurist premillennialism is not that and must not be billed for it. Separate the system from the circus.
terms.homeworkArc: One page, four columns. As each map is drawn, note the single text it handles best and the single text it handles worst. All four columns must have both by the end.

units.label: The Day of the LORD, where the language starts
Olivet, read the Term One way
Caught up: what 1 Thessalonians actually says
Israel and the church, one more time

terms.title: Isaiah: The Servant Songs
terms.kick: PROPHETS · the arm of the LORD revealed
terms.rationale: After the maps, a face. Isaiah's Servant songs are the deepest well in the prophets: a servant who is Israel, and then somehow more than Israel, who wins by being struck, whose disfigurement heals. Three full days in chapter fifty-three because it will not be rushed. Then Isaiah's own new heavens and new earth, which is where John got the language you will walk in two terms. This is the term where doctrine goes quiet and beauty does the arguing.

units.label: The sustained tongue, the struck back
The year of the LORD's favor
New heavens, in Isaiah's own mouth

terms.title: Ecclesiastes
terms.kick: WISDOM SHORT · vapor, and what to do about it
terms.rationale: A book for a cynic, announced for the self-described pragmatist. Qoheleth ran your experiment — money, work, pleasure, building projects — with a bigger budget than you will ever have, and filed his report: vapor. Not meaningless; vapor. Real, and ungraspable, and gone by noon. This is the Bible's own answer to the man who distrusts hype, and it is more severe than your cynicism and more hopeful than your pragmatism. Eight days. Eat your bread, drink your wine, fear God. The end of the matter has been heard.

units.label: Oppression, envy, a second pair of hands
God is in heaven, you are on earth
Bread on the waters, light is sweet

terms.title: Revelation: The City Comes Down
terms.kick: HOPE · the apocalypse, with the maps in hand
terms.rationale: You drew the maps three terms ago. Now walk the territory. Revelation, read as what it is — apocalyptic, pastoral, written to seven real churches under a boot — and not as a code to crack. The cycles of judgment are read whole and they are heavy. But keep your eye on the direction of travel at the end, because it settles your question: nobody escapes up and out. The city comes down. The kings carry their glory into it. Heaven comes here, which is what you suspected, said more carefully than you have been saying it.
terms.hardNote: The seal, trumpet, and bowl cycles are read as written, and Revelation 14:9-11 with them. The Lamb is also the Judge, and the book does not apologize for it.

units.label: The rider, the millennium, the judgment

terms.title: The Puritans
terms.kick: CHURCH HISTORY · your confession had authors
terms.rationale: Your confession had authors, and they are this term. The 1689 was written by men worshiping illegally — Kiffin, Knollys, Keach — while Owen and Baxter published a few streets away. Owen's line belongs beside Term Twenty-Two: be killing sin, or it will be killing you. We take their devotion and their failures together, conformity wars and all, because a tradition you cannot criticize is a tradition you do not actually know. Eight days. Take what is gold.
terms.secondNote: This is family history for him specifically: the 1689 framers were Puritans. Make the line from Term 20's document to these men's lives explicit.

units.label: Who they were, what they wanted
Bunyan: the pilgrim in the jail

terms.title: 1 Corinthians Whole
terms.kick: EPISTLE · one church, every problem
terms.rationale: One church, every problem you have studied, all at once. Corinth had factions, a lawsuit, a scandal the pagans found embarrassing, chaos at the Supper, and a gifts controversy — and Paul loved them and said so in the first paragraph. This is where Term Fifteen's chapters go back into their context: twelve, thirteen, and fourteen were never three topics, they are one argument, and love is its hinge. It ends on resurrection and a working man's promise: therefore, your labor is not in vain.
terms.hardNote: Chapters 5 and 6 are read whole: the incest case, the command to expel, the lawsuit aired in public. Church discipline is in the Bible and it is uncomfortable on purpose.

units.label: Idol meat and the weaker brother
Gifts in context, love in context
Raised how, and the last word

terms.title: The World Renewed: Work and Vocation
terms.kick: PRACTICE SHORT · labor that is not in vain
terms.rationale: Six days on the promise that closed last term. You run operations, you build systems, you are far from your passport country building a life — which is exactly the exile's assignment from Term Ten: build houses, plant gardens, seek the city's good. Here is your heaven-and-earth instinct in its sane form. You do not build the kingdom up to God; the city comes down. But what is done in the Lord survives the fire and follows you in. Work like that is true. So work like that.

units.label: Made to work: the garden mandate

terms.title: The Minor Prophets
terms.kick: PROPHETS · twelve men, one complaint
terms.rationale: Twelve men, one complaint: you have forgotten. Hosea is told to marry the complaint. Jonah embodies it. Habakkuk files it against God himself and receives the line that lit the Reformation: the righteous shall live by faith. The Day of the LORD language you studied in the four maps was minted here. This is the sweep term, a dozen voices in twelve days, and it is heavy in places, because God's grief usually is. Malachi ends it with a sunrise and four hundred years of silence.
terms.hardNote: Hosea 1-3 is read whole: God commands a marriage to unfaithfulness to make his own grief visible. Nahum's celebration of Nineveh's fall is read as written.

terms.title: The Church You're Actually In
terms.kick: PRACTICE · the pew you actually sit in
terms.rationale: The last term of the plan, and it is about the pew you actually sit in. Three years of study have sharpened your convictions — covenantal, credobaptist, Reformed — and you worship, gladly, in a dispensational church, having been raised in the faith by charismatics. Some men resolve that by leaving, some by going quiet, some by getting sharp. This term is the fourth way: real membership, honest triage of what divides and what must not, submission to elders you partly disagree with, and gratitude, by name, for the people you came from. One body. Attain it.
terms.secondNote: This term is the biographical payoff of the whole plan. Charismatic years, dispensational pulpit, covenantal bookshelf — the curriculum sharpened every difference on purpose, and this term teaches him to hold sharpened convictions with an unsharpened tongue.
terms.homeworkArc: By the last day: one letter, one page, never sent or maybe sent — to someone from your charismatic years, thanking them for something specific they gave you.
